name: Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN)
note: Uganda's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: the Uganda Revenue Authority assigns every taxpayer a TIN; anyone likely to do tax business with it must apply; ten digits, nine sequential and a check digit by a modulus-97 rule the game doesn't compute (`check` left out), assigned free of charge. Read as given on application, to anyone, at no fee. No age or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Uganda: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: Any person who is likely to transact in any tax related business with URA, shall be required to apply for a TIN. ... The TIN is a ten-digit numeric identifier assigned free of charge ... a) The first nine digits represent a sequentially assigned number. b) The final digit serves as a check digit
